compute.reported_as: Energy results achieved by wave-functions before and after a Lanczos step are evaluated with the MC sample number in the magnitude of O(4.5×10^4). [Sec. III] ... (1) With a sample size of O(4.5×10^4), the step size is initially set to 2×10^−3 and then reduced to 2×10^−4. (2) With a sample size of O(4.5×10^4), the step size is initially set to 2×10^−3, the sample size is then increased to O(4.5×10^5) while maintaining the step size, and finally, the step size is reduced to 2×10^−4. ... For lattices larger than 64 sites, both strategies require no more than 2×10^4 optimization steps to achieve full convergence. [Sec. III.A] ... X. Liang thanks Eric J. Walter for resource allocations on the William & Mary Sciclone cluster. The author acknowledges William & Mary Research Computing and the Texas Advanced Computing Center (TACC) at The University of Texas at Austin for providing computational resources that have contributed to the results reported within this paper. Part of numerical results were obtained on the Bridges-2 at Pittsburgh Supercomputing Center through allocation (phy240244). [Sec. V Acknowledgement]
compute.source: Sec. III (opening), Sec. III.A Optimization details, Sec. V Acknowledgement, arXiv:2507.01856 (compute pass 2026-09-16)
compute.note: No device, GPU/CPU count, wall-clock or core-hours stated anywhere (main text, Tables I-VII, Figs. 1-14 captions, Appendices A-D); the acknowledgement names the Sciclone, TACC and Bridges-2 clusters without quantities. samples = order-of-magnitude statement O(4.5×10^4) for energy evaluation (optimization used O(4.5e4) rising to O(4.5e5) in strategy 2; 46,080 samples are quoted for structure factors in App. B / Fig. 8). iterations = stated upper bound only: "no more than 2×10^4 optimization steps" for lattices larger than 64 sites (Sec. III.A); also "fewer than 2×10^4 optimization steps" for the Table II results.
